Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem, like a set of Russian dolls nested inside each other.  
Each call works on a simpler case until it reaches a "base case"—a condition so simple that the function returns an answer without calling itself again.  
For example, to compute the factorial of 5, you compute 5 × factorial(4), which needs factorial(3), and so on down to factorial(1) = 1.  
The key is to ensure every recursive call moves closer to the base case, or the function will loop forever and crash.
